parsed_answer.content: Java 21 introduces Structured Concurrency (Preview) and Scoped Values as transformative paradigms designed to replace error-prone, unstructured asynchronous programming models like ExecutorService and CompletableFuture. Structured concurrency treats groups of related concurrent tasks running in different threads as a single unit of work, ensuring robust cancellation propagation, error handling, and clean lexical lifetimes. Simultaneously, Scoped Values provide a modern, immutable, and thread-safe alternative to ThreadLocal variables. While ThreadLocal allows mutable data to be shared globally within a thread, it suffers from severe memory leaks, unbounded mutability, and high overhead when dealing with millions of virtual threads. Scoped Values bind a value to a specific code block, guaranteeing that the data is strictly immutable, securely bound, and automatically reclaimed as soon as the scope exits, making them uniquely suited for high-throughput, virtual-thread-based architectures.

items: StructuredTaskScope enforces a strict containment rule: child threads spawned within a scope must complete before the scope's block exits, preventing runaway threads and resource leaks.

When using StructuredTaskScope.ShutdownOnFailure, the failure of any subtask automatically signals cancellation to all other concurrent subtasks, cutting short unnecessary CPU cycles and I/O operations.

Scoped Values utilize a carrier-thread-based underlying binding mechanism that scales effortlessly to millions of virtual threads, contrasting sharply with ThreadLocal's per-thread ThreadLocalMap which frequently causes OOM errors under high thread churn.

parsed_answer.content: Production Gotcha: Because Structured Concurrency and Scoped Values are heavily tied to Project Loom's virtual threads, never use blocking synchronization primitives like synchronized blocks or legacy ReentrantLocks inside ScopedValue scopes if they trigger pin-ning. Pinning forces the virtual thread to monopolize its carrier thread, defeating the massive throughput advantages you gain by combining structured concurrency with Scoped Values.
